faqs.question: What is the Zeiss Stemi 355 used for?
faqs.answer: It's a compact stereo microscope for classroom teaching, biology lab dissection, and industrial inspection, viewing specimens in three dimensions without any sample preparation.

faqs.question: What are the three configurations?
faqs.answer: Education, Labs, and Industry, each a ready-to-use set matched to its setting, with a different illumination system built in.

faqs.question: Does the specimen need to be prepared before viewing?
faqs.answer: No. Stemi 355 observes specimens in their natural state, no slides, staining, or coverslips required.

faqs.question: What illumination does each set include?
faqs.answer: Education has an LED spot for strong-shadow detail and a flat transmitted light base. Labs has a double-arm gooseneck for adjustable oblique lighting and a tiltable mirror base. Industry has a segmentable LED ringlight for shadow-free or oblique inspection.

faqs.question: Is the Industry set safe for electronics work?
faqs.answer: Yes, it includes ESD properties, an antistatic coating on the microscope body and stand.

faqs.question: Can images be captured and documented?
faqs.answer: Yes, an optional microscope camera attaches to the phototube for instant capture and sharing.

faqs.question: How many stand and tube options are available?
faqs.answer: Three stands and two tube options, which assemble into the configuration that fits the application.

faqs.question: Is Stemi 355 replacing another Zeiss model?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's the successor to Stemi 305, which is reaching end of sales shortly.

faqs.question: Is there a return policy?
faqs.answer: Yes, a 60-day risk-free purchase. If it isn't the right fit, it can be returned with no questions asked.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Full technical specifications, including magnification range, objective set and zoom ratio, are available from Inkarp on request.

faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the configuration selected.

sections.title: Three Sets, Three Jobs
sections.tabSummary: Choosing between Education, Labs, and Industry
body: Compare the Education, Laboratory, and Industry versions of the ZEISS Stemi 355 Stereo Microscope to choose the right configuration.

A stereo microscope built for a classroom doesn't need ESD protection, and one built for an electronics bench doesn't need to survive being carried between rooms every hour. Stemi 355 doesn't try to do all three jobs with one fixed setup, it ships as three distinct sets, each matched to the environment it'll actually live in.

Education is built to travel: easy to transport, easy to install, easy to use, with an LED spot for the strong-shadow detail that makes a specimen's texture obvious to a room full of students. Labs adds a double-arm gooseneck for variable oblique lighting, precisely the control a dissection actually needs as the angle of a cut changes. Industry swaps that gooseneck for a segmentable ringlight, shadow-free when the inspection needs even coverage, switchable to oblique segments when a defect needs raking light to show up, all on an ESD-safe body.

sections.title: Illumination Built for the Specimen
sections.description: Learn how the illumination options of the ZEISS Stemi 355 Stereo Microscope improve contrast and specimen visibility.

cards.title: Strong shadow for surface texture, classroom setting
Adjustable shadow through an active dissection
Shadow-free overview, switchable to oblique for defects
Standard brightfield/darkfield across all settings
cards.description: Transmitted light base, all three sets

paragraphs: A stereo microscope's value often comes down to how well the light reveals texture, not just magnification. Flat, even light flattens detail; the wrong shadow angle hides it. Stemi 355's three illumination systems exist because different specimens need genuinely different light.

The LED spot on the Education set throws strong shadow specifically to make surface texture obvious, ideal for a first look at an insect's exoskeleton or a leaf's structure. The double-arm gooseneck on the Labs set gives that same shadow control but with two independently positioned arms, letting a dissection adjust lighting angle as the specimen itself changes shape under the tools. The segmentable ringlight on the Industry set does the opposite job when needed, even, shadow-free light for a clean overview, with the option to switch to oblique segments the moment a defect needs raking light to actually show itself.

faqs.question: What is the Zeiss Stemi 508 used for?
faqs.answer: It's a high-performance Greenough stereo microscope for detailed 3D inspection and documentation, used across biological research, industrial QC, and materials analysis.

faqs.question: What is the magnification range?
faqs.answer: 2x to 250x, using interchangeable apochromatic front optics and eyepieces, with an 8:1 zoom ratio.

faqs.question: What does apochromatic mean for the image?
faqs.answer: It removes color fringing, delivering high-contrast, distortion-free images across the full zoom range.

faqs.question: What is the working distance?
faqs.answer: Up to 287 mm, giving room to work under the objective without compromising optical quality.

faqs.question: What is the field of view?
faqs.answer: Up to 122 mm.

faqs.question: Is the viewing angle comfortable for long sessions?
faqs.answer: Yes, a 35° viewing angle is designed to keep posture relaxed even across hours of continuous use.

faqs.question: Can the zoom be locked at fixed magnifications?
faqs.answer: Yes, click-stop mode provides reproducible magnification steps, alongside continuously variable zoom, with focus staying sharp across either mode.

faqs.question: What stand options are available?
faqs.answer: Stand M with memory function for up to three illumination setups, Stand K as a compact all-in-one unit, Stand N with a large base for big samples, and boom stands for flexible positioning.

faqs.question: Does it support polarization contrast?
faqs.answer: Yes, with gliding, tilting, or rotating polarization stages available.

faqs.question: Can a camera be attached?
faqs.answer: Yes, Stemi 508 doc includes a c-mount adapter for ZEISS Axiocam cameras as standard, interchangeable to adapt SLR cameras or camcorders.

faqs.question: How is Stemi 508 different from Stemi 355?
faqs.answer: Stemi 508 adds apochromatic zoom optics, an 8:1 zoom ratio, a documented 2x–250x magnification range, working distances up to 287 mm, and polarization contrast, positioning it above Stemi 355's entry-level, fixed-configuration routine inspection range.

Swap front optics and eyepieces, and magnification runs from 2x to 250x, with working distances stretching to 287 mm, room to actually work under the objective without the optics losing quality. Zoom continuously, or lock into reproducible click stops, and the image stays sharply focused across the whole range either way. A 35° viewing angle keeps posture comfortable through hours at the eyepiece. Choose from compact stands to flexible boom stands, and from basic transmitted light through polarization contrast, built to fit exactly what the application needs. What it delivers: color-accurate, distortion-free 3D imaging across a genuinely wide zoom range. What it doesn't cost you: working distance, comfort, or optical quality at either end of the range. What it succeeds from and pairs with: the entry-level Stemi 355, one step down in the same range.

sections.title: Apochromatic Optics and the 8:1 Zoom
sections.tabSummary: What color accuracy and range actually mean in use
body: What color accuracy and range actually mean at the eyepiece.

Standard stereo optics show color fringing at high magnification, a soft halo around edges that gets worse the further you zoom in. That's not a minor cosmetic issue when the work depends on distinguishing genuine material boundaries from optical artifacts. Apochromatic correction removes it, at every point across Stemi 508's zoom range.

The 8:1 zoom ratio means that correction holds from a 122 mm field of view down to the finest detail an interchangeable eyepiece and front optic combination can resolve, up to 250x. And because working distance stretches to 287 mm at the wide end, reaching that level of detail doesn't mean crowding tools, hands, or a soldering iron into a cramped gap under the objective.

cards.title: Switching between several standard setups regularly
Large specimens or big industrial parts
Sample position that varies, or needs flexible reach

paragraphs: A stereo microscope stand is as much about the sample as the optics sitting above it, a Petri dish, a large industrial casting, and a component that needs a hands-free boom arm all demand genuinely different mechanical setups.

Stand M stores up to three illumination setups and recalls them instantly, with LED already built into the M LED variant, ideal for a lab switching between several standard procedures. Stand K is a compact all-in-one unit for straightforward bench use. Stand N carries a large base built specifically for bigger specimens or industrial workpieces. Boom stands trade a fixed footprint for flexibility, positioning the optics wherever the workplace and sample space actually demand.
